vocab.definition: fully ionised in water, e.g. HCl, H₂SO₄.
only partially ionised, e.g. ethanoic, citric.
the amount of acid dissolved per dm³.
the splitting of a molecule into ions in water.

misconceptions.wrong: Strong and concentrated mean the same.
misconceptions.right: Strong = fully ionised; concentrated = lots dissolved.
A weak acid can still be very concentrated.

misconceptions.wrong: Weak acids do not fully react.
misconceptions.right: They react fully, just more slowly / lower H⁺.

infoPanels.title: STRONG vs WEAK
workedSteps: Same concentration → strong acid has lower pH.

questions.text: State what is meant by a strong acid. [1 mark]
Explain the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid. [2 marks]
Two acids have the same concentration. Explain why the strong acid has a lower pH. [2 marks]
If pH falls from 4 to 2, state how the H⁺ concentration changes. [1 mark]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: A strong acid is ______ ionised; a weak acid is only ______ ionised.

questions.text: Classify each as strong or weak: HCl, citric acid, H₂SO₄. [3 marks]

footer.tip: Strength = how much it ionises. Concentration = how much is dissolved.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why can a dilute strong acid have the same pH as a concentrated weak acid?
